<reason>A offered the stronger comparative mechanism: political fear suppresses defensible context beyond targeted materials and leaves losses harder to detect and correct. B legitimately challenged prevalence, but repeatedly equated poor visibility with unknowability and asserted documented, irreversible content harms without establishing that comparison. Although A's magnitude claim remained inferential, it answered the pressure questions directly and better explained why self-censorship threatens both accurate understanding and correction.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A defeated B's distinction between harmless gaps and durable false beliefs: omissions can themselves create misleading understanding. Its closing then exposed the causal error in B's response—calling that misunderstanding a content defect does not erase the political self-censorship that produced it.</best_rebuttal>
